paper_title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for   Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
caption: Number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods has at least 1 factual error. Factual errors: < OneR < NoR.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled "Factual Errors" displays the number of questions (out of 40) in which the chain-of-thought (CoT) generated by GPT-3 using three different methods—NoR QA (yellow with grid pattern), OneR QA (red with dot pattern), and IRCot QA (blue with diagonal stripes)—contained at least one factual error, across four different question datasets: HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order, while the vertical axis represents the count of questions with factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. For each dataset, three bars are grouped together, corresponding to the three QA methods. In HotpotQA, the counts are 15 (NoR QA), 10 (OneR QA), and 5 (IRCot QA). In 2WikiMQA, the values are 29 (NoR QA), 23 (OneR QA), and 14 (IRCot QA). For MuSiQue, the counts are 28 (NoR QA), 27 (OneR QA), and 23 (IRCot QA). In IIRC, the values are 15 (NoR QA), 14 (OneR QA), and 11 (IRCot QA). The bars are arranged in the same order for each dataset, and the heights are proportional to the numerical values, with NoR QA consistently showing the highest number of factual errors, followed by OneR QA, and then IRCot QA, as noted in the caption. The chart visually confirms the trend that factual errors are most frequent in NoR QA, followed by OneR QA, and least in IRCot QA.
